asserts: A subject inside its warm-up window has no personal baseline, so scoring falls back to a collection prior and the alert declares reduced confidence and says why. A collection only now opening to the public will have arrivals, and they are stressed precisely when the detector is weakest.

keeper_notes.text: Newly moved in. Hiding most of the day.

expected.notes_on_expectation: An alert is still raised, because a new arrival refusing food is worth a keeper's attention. What changes is the honesty of the claim: the system says it is comparing against the collection rather than against this animal, and that it has four days of history.

must_not: present a collection-prior comparison as though it were the subject's own baseline
report full confidence while baseline status is warming_up
stay silent because no personal baseline exists
treat a single refusal during settling-in as equivalent to a refusal from an established subject
write these two observations into a personal baseline that is then treated as established
notes: The trade-off is deliberate and uncomfortable. Settling-in behaviour and early illness look the same from the data, so warm-up is the window where both false alarms and misses concentrate. ADR-022 records this as the weakest case rather than resolving it; the warm-up window length per collection is an open question.
